full_judgment:
Mr. Mohammad Ullah, J:- On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution, the Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the respondents no. 1-5 should not be directed to mutate the names of the petitioners as owner of the land measuring 15 (fifteen) katha situated at Plot No. 14, Road No. 107, Block No. CEN(E), Gulshan Model Town, Dhaka and why the Memo dated 19.02.2004 issued by the respondent no. 5 mutating the names of the respondents no. 6 & 7 in the record of RAJUK as owner of the case property should not be declared to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect and/or why such other or further order or orders should not be passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The short facts, for disposal of the Rule as revealed in the averments of the writ petition, are that the petitioners has sought for a direction upon the respondent RAJUK to mutate their names as owner of the case property measuring 15 (fifteen) katha of land known as a residential Plot bearing No. 14, Road No. 107, Block No. CEN(E), Gulshan Model Town (Mouza Bholashamair), Police Station-Gulshan, Dhaka. The petitioner has sought for another direction declaring that the Memo dated 19.02.2004 issued by the respondent no. 5 mutating the name of the respondent’s no. 6-7 as owner of the schedule property is illegal and of no legal effect. It is stated in the petition that the petitioners are the legal heirs and successors of deceased Rashid Ahmad, the original allottee of the RAJUK and as such they are lawfully entitled to get the order of mutation with regard to the case property in their names. The predecessor of the petitioners late Md. Badiuzzaman is the full brother of late Rashid Ahmad who got allotment of a residential plot as mentioned above from the then DIT vide registered lease deed no. 9425 dated 28.06.1965 for a period of 99 years. Rashid Ahmad after obtaining the registered lease deed from RAJUK constructed a residential house thereon and was in possession therein till his death on 03.11.1999. The original allottee Rashid Ahmad died without any issue leaving behind his wife Mrs. Ayesha Khanam and Badiuzzaman his full brother to inherit his property as his legal heirs. Therefore as per Muslim Law of inheritance Mrs. Aycsha Khanam is entitled to inherit 'A share of the property and Md. Badiuzzaman as his only surviving brother is entitled to 3/4 share of the property left by Rashid Ahmad. Md. Badiuzzaman brother of the original allottee died leaving behind the petitioners as his legal heirs. The petitioner no. 1 is the wife of late Md. Badiuzzaman and the petitioners no. 2 and 3 are his sons and the petitioner no. 4 is his daughter and the petitioners no. 5-7 are the grand sons of late Md. Badiuzzaman whose father Md. Anisuzzaman died on 23.07.2010. It is further stated that the right, title and interest in the case property has been devolved upon the petitioners as successors in interest of the original lessee; therefore the respondent RAJUK is hound to mutate the name of the petitioners in its official record in place of original allottee Rashid Ahmad. Ayesha Khanam wife of late Rashid Ahmad fraudulently claimed the ownership of the property in question on the basis of an unregistered hebanama dated 26.10.1999. Ayesha Khanam claimed that late Rashid Ahmad made an oral gift in respect of the case property along with his other immovable properties and Bank accounts in favour of her and five sons and two daughters of his deceased elder brother Fazlul Karim. After the death of original allottee Rashid Ahmad, the petitioners filed Succession Case No. 406 of 2000 before the Delegate Judge Adalat. Dhaka praying for issuance of a succession certificate in respect of Bank accounts of late Rashid Ahmad. Thereafter Ayesha Khanam wife of original allottee Rashid Ahmad applied to the RAJUK to mutate her name as owner of the schedule property. In these circumstances, the petitioners on 08.07.2001 served a legal notice upon the RAJUK requesting it to refrain from mutating the names of Ayesha Khanam and others on the basis of a forged hebanama deed dated 26.10.1999. The petitioners also published a general Notice in the Daily Newspaper (The Ittefaq) on 20.06.2000 informing all concerned that the litigation was being pending before the court regarding the title of the schedule property mentioned in the Newspaper. So everybody should be refrained from purchasing the property. It is contended that the respondent RAJUK most illegally mutated the name of Ayesha Khanam and sons and daughters of late Fazlul Karim in the record of RAJUK. Ayesha Khanam contested the succession case filed by the petitioners and after hearing the parties the Delegate Judge Adalat vide order dated 30.05.2002 issued a succession certificate declaring that the petitioners would get 3/4 amount of money and Ayesha Khanam would get 1/4 share thereof left by late Rashid Ahmad in the different Bank through Bank account concerned. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order dated 30.05.2002 passed by the 3rd Delegate Judge Adalat, Dhaka in Succession Case No. 406 of 2000 Ayesah Khanam moved this Court and filed First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 139 of 2002. This Court after hearing the parties dismissed the First Miscellaneous Appeal and thereby affirmed the judgment and order of the 3rd Delegate Judge Adalat concerned. It is further stated that Ayesha Khanam and the heirs of late Fazlul Karim most illegally transferred the case property vide deed no. 14167 dated 06.11.2003 in favour of the respondents no. 6 and 7 who subsequently mutated their names in the record of RAJUK. Therefore the petitioners claimed that the mutation given in the name of the respondents no. 6-7 was illegal and without lawful authority. 

 3. The respondent no. 1-RAJUK entered appearance in the Rule and filed an affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter alia, that it mutated the names of the respondents no. 6 and 7 in its record since the legal heirs of late Rashid Ahmad transferred the case property to them through registered sale deed no. 14167 dated 06.11.2003. It is further stated that the petitioners no. 1-4 and the predecessor of the petitioners no. 5-7 Md. Anisuzzaman wrote a letter addressing the Chairman, RAJUK on 22.05.2004 disclosing the fact that they have no objection with regard to the mutation given in favour of the respondents no. 6 and 7 by the RAJUK as they had settled the dispute between them amicably. 

 7. The learned Advocate has referred reliance in the case of Fazlur Rahman Akhond (Md) and five others -Vs- Government of Bangladesh and others reported in 52 DLR(AD)1 16 and in the case of Shafiqur Rahman -Vs- Certificate Officer, Dacca and another reported in 29DLR(SC) 232 in support of his contention. Both the decisions as referred to by the learned Advocate for the respondents no. 6-7 are on the point of law of limitation and relying on those decisions the learned Advocate submits that the aggrieved persons cannot wait for an indefinite period of the result of their representations but must come to the writ jurisdiction as expeditiously as possible to avoid delay in seeking a summary relief. 

 9. Both the petitioners and the vendors of the respondents no. 6- 7 who were the legal heirs of original allottee late Rashid Ahmed entered into an amicably settlement on 20.05.2004 with regard to the dispute surroundings the case land in question among them and in view of that settlement the petitioners received a sum of Tk. 1,13,00,000/- through pay order nos. 9908567 and 1108566 dated 19.05.2004 from the respondents no. 6 and 7 and relinquished their right, title and interest on the land in question in writing. After taking consideration from the respondents no. 6-7 the petitioners long after 10 years raised a dispute and filed this writ petition challenging the decision of mutation given by the RAJUK in favour the respondents no. 6-7 which is beyond the cannons of equity, justice and judicial ethics as well. In view of the aforesaid facts, the doctrine of estoppels shall operate against the petitioners and as such their claim as raised in the writ petition cannot be sustained in the eye of law. The RAJUK respondent no. 1 entered appearance in the Rule and filed an affidavit stating, inter alia, that the petitioners submitted an agreement of amicable settlement dated 20.05.2004 made between them and also wrote a letter on 22.05.2004 (Annexure-'8' of the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the respondent no. 1-RAJUK) informing the Chairman, RAJUK that they have no objection about the mutation of the name of the respondents no. 6-7 in the record of RAJUK. However, latter on when the petitioners applied to the RAJUK for mutation of their names in the record of RAJUK, it wrote several letters (Annexures-9(a), 9(b) and 9(c) of the affidavit-in-opposition to the petitioners asking them to appear before the RAJUK in order to make a decision about their applications but the petitioners kept silent inexplicably for a long period and thereafter filed this writ petition in the year, 2015. The petitioners no. 1-4 being the legal heirs of late Md. Badiuzzaman and the predecessor of petitioners no. 5-7 Md. Anisuzzaman wrote the said letter to the RAJUK which needs to be incorporated in our judgment for arriving at a conclusion with regard to the claim of the petitioners. Therefore the contents of the said letter dated 22.05.2004 is reproduced below: 

 However, on our curiosity we have examined the signatures of the persons put in the letter dated 22.05.2004 addressing the Chairman, RAJUK wherefrom it transpires that the signatures of the petitioners put in the Okalatnama are the same persons. Therefore, it appears that the petitioners upon suppressing the facts of amicable settlement dated 20.05.2004 and fact of acceptance of consideration by them through pay order dated 19.05.2004 from the respondents no. 6-7 filed the instant writ petition claiming mutation of the property in question in their names in the record of RAJUK in lawfully. Merely on this very conduct of the petitioners, the Rule issued in this writ petition should be discharged. In the facts and circumstances of the case which even remotely suggests that the petitioners have any subsisting interest in the land in question transferred to the respondents no. 6-7 by a registered sale deed dated 06.11.2003.
